what_its_for: Hydralazine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It relaxes and widens your blood vessels, making it easier for your heart to pump blood and helping to lower your blood pressure. It may also be used for heart failure in some patients.
how_to_take: Take hydralazine by mouth with or without food. Taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this could cause your blood pressure to spike dangerously high.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how your body responds. The typical starting dose is 10 mg taken 4 times a day (every 6 hours). Your doctor may increase your dose up to 50 mg taken 4 times a day if needed. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store hydralazine tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking hydralazine, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and make you feel dizzy or faint. Be careful when standing up quickly from a sitting or lying position, as this medicine may cause dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Limit your intake of very salty foods, as excess salt can make this medicine less effective at controlling your blood pressure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe chest pain or a fast or pounding heartbeat; severe headache, dizziness, or fainting; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles; joint pain, muscle aches, or a skin rash (especially a butterfly-shaped rash on your face, which could be a sign of a rare condition called drug-induced lupus); numbness or tingling in your hands or feet; fever or feeling very unwell; or if your blood pressure readings are still very high. Seek emergency help immediately if you experience signs of a stroke such as sudden weakness on one side of the body, slurred speech, or vision changes.
when_it_works: Hydralazine starts to lower your blood pressure within 20 to 30 minutes after taking a dose. However, it may take several weeks of regular use for your blood pressure to be fully controlled and for you to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Keep taking it even if you feel fine, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Continue monitoring your blood pressure at home or at your doctor's office as directed.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medicine, increasing your risk of dizziness and falls. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Pregnancy: Hydralazine is sometimes used during pregnancy to treat dangerously high blood pressure, but only under close medical supervision. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose, as this medicine is processed by these organs. Always inform your doctor of all your medical conditions and all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
